title: Self-Deprecation Restraint
text: “Welcome back, Motoyasu-kun, Itsuki, everyone. How’d it go?”
“An easy victory, I say.”
“We wrapped things up before the kingdom’s people could even show up. It was easy enough to be startling, honestly. Made me realize all over again just how foolish my past behavior must have been.”
“It was like this constantly, exhaustingly so. Iwatani-sama, you really ought to stop spoiling Bow Hero so much, or this’ll just keep happening, won’t it?”

“Hmm… well, Itsuki, don’t you think it’s about time you let go of the self-deprecating jokes? I get that you might not be able to forgive your past self, but if you don’t forgive yourself eventually, I’m worried you’ll break down someday. Emia-san and Rishia-san are hoping for that too, you know.”
At Father’s gentle words, Itsuki looked away, seeming apologetic.
“…Coming from Naofumi-san of all people, I suppose I’ll make an effort.”
It seemed Itsuki was going to try to restrain himself from self-deprecating remarks going forward.

“Well, I’m glad things seem fine as far as Melromarc goes. As for the waves brewing over in Siltvelt and Zeltoble, we’ve already arranged to quietly deal with those too. Motoyasu-kun and the others can rest if you want—what do you say?”
“Something like that hardly counts as tiring. I just rode around on a Filolial the whole time.”
“Got it. Though, Wolf and the others do want to cut loose and fight for the sake of the world, so… keep in mind you might end up on standby instead.”
“Yes, I’m not so uncouth as to steal someone else’s moment to shine. Though I hear some spear-wielder somewhere went and did something rather uncouth.”
“Whoever could you mean?”
I thought I heard Father’s voice mutter you, it’s you, but surely that was just my imagination.
“…So, the wave in Melromarc is still going to end up chalked up as my achievement again, huh.”
Ren, dragging along Luna-chan and Keel, grumbled like he had a bone to pick.

“Well, since you’ve gotten away clean on that front, I figure crediting it to Motoyasu-kun and Itsuki works fine. Something like, after crushing the Three Heroes Church’s conspiracy in Melromarc, the country went out of control, but the heroes still fulfilled their duty—that kind of narrative should hold up.”
“I see, then make absolutely sure it goes that way! Don’t you dare pin my achievements on some me that isn’t actually me!”
Ren seemed awfully desperate about it. And so, rather than concentrating the wave’s credit entirely on Ren, it ended up getting distributed among the rest of us instead.
“Well… all that’s left is hoping the unrest in Melromarc settles down.”

“Will it, though? Given how things looked, it seemed like nothing short of exterminating the enemy of all mankind, Shield Hero, would satisfy them. So presumably they’ll march on Siltvelt following that logic, get counterattacked, and be wiped out. Yeah, I can see it.”
Itsuki gave a soft, mocking chuckle, still as sarcastic as ever.
“The domestic forces are already worn down to a dangerous point—attacking from there seems impossible, don’t you think? Besides, the king’s probably got bigger problems than that right now anyway.”

“I wonder. If anything, I honestly can’t see where this is supposed to land… ah, though there’s a faint hope that if King Azott spoke up against the fighting, some of the public might listen, given how his approval ratings play into it.”

Thinking back on the good deeds Father had done, it seemed plausible that some people would actually listen. But then again, I had a feeling that this time, it wouldn’t be Ren—rather, Rafumi disguised as Ren—whose reputation would take a hit from some incident. And Ren’s companions had apparently spotted Rival, judging by the faces they were making, like they had something to report to Ren.
“Um…”
“What is it?”
“Er… well…”
There was no need to say anything unnecessary regarding Rival. That thing’s existence was nothing but a nuisance, after all.
“Anyway, good work, everyone. I made food for everyone who took part in the wave. Take it easy today.”
“Yaaay!”
“Foooood~”
And so, the Filolial-samas and the rest of those who’d taken part in the wave ate the exquisite meal Father and the others had prepared, and were thoroughly satisfied.
And so… the day after the second wave had ended.
“The wave’s been put down, and there’s not much left to do within Melromarc… but waiting for an opening has its own kind of boredom to it, doesn’t it.”

I recalled that when the loop had restarted, Takt had already finished off Ren and Itsuki, so we’d been busy cleaning up the remnants of that mess. One way or another, Father—currently posing as an apprentice to a monster dealer—had built up quite the network of connections in Zeltoble by now. Given that he was steadily sending reliable fighters into the Colosseum too, it might soon be time for him to graduate from apprentice and strike out on his own. Come to think of it, that meant both the falsely accused Father and the ever-kind Father were each on their way to becoming a merchant known throughout Zeltoble. Truly, Father was something else.
“What I do won’t change. Travel around, harvest the so-called superior beings known as humans, and send them off to where they rightfully belong.”
“Itsuki… I really wish you’d learn your lesson by now…”
“Even so, it’s a fact that there are people out there stirring up trouble, isn’t it?”

“That part’s true, sure… but I can’t exactly say assassinating them is the right call. I mean… honestly, I think even the people of Melromarc are getting worn out by now, don’t you? Hating someone endlessly is exhausting work.”
“I’m not the least bit tired, personally.”
“Not very convincing, coming from someone everyone’s worried is wearing thin.”
At Father’s words, Itsuki looked like he wanted to argue back, but fell silent instead, faced with the worried looks from Mole and Riska.
“Father, there’s something I’m curious about—might I ask?”
“What is it?”
“Hasn’t your standing in Zeltoble improved quite a bit by now?”

“Huh? Well, sure, I’ve taken on various commissions from the slave trader, gotten Shion and Wolf to fight in the Colosseum, and Sadeena-san occasionally shows up on a whim too. On top of that, I’ve been running a proper, wholesome circus business on the side.”
“Then, would it be possible to strike indirectly at Melromarc’s underbelly by way of Zeltoble?”
Father seemed to mull it over when I asked him that.

“I mean, it is a rather bloody topic, but… yeah, there do seem to be organizations that’ll take on dangerous work like that so long as you pay enough. Slipping operatives into the Three Heroes Church for assassination or intelligence gathering—that kind of thing might be doable.”
“One way or another, Naofumi-san sure has connections to some shady organizations, doesn’t he.”
“Itsukiii… don’t you realize that if you go sneaking into some noble’s mansion, enslave people, and quietly sell them off, connections like that just naturally come along with it?”
Father said this with a smile, pinching and stretching Itsuki’s cheek.
“Mmmph—stop that! Th-there’s no pain, but scolding me by stretching this pouch-like cheek of mine—you really don’t hold back, Naofumi-san.”
“What kind of compliment is that supposed to be, Itsuki. Anyway… it’s a dangerous topic, but indirect information gathering or assassination requests aren’t impossible, no. But why bring this up?”
“Both Ren and I are capable of assassination ourselves. I was simply curious just how far Zeltoble’s reach extends, so I asked.”
“Naofumi-san. You have connections with information brokers in Zeltoble, don’t you? Could you look into Usaunny? If you’ve got connections like that, investigating would be the fastest route.”
Yikes, I thought. If an information broker existed who could dig that up, it would be instantly obvious that Usaunny was the name of a fairy from the frontier settlement.
“I could try asking, sure, but… I wonder if they’d actually find anything. Also, casually mentioning you’re good at assassination like that…”
Ugh… with Rival already sniffing around, was it only a matter of time before Usaunny’s true identity got exposed?
“I bet Ren-san is looking for her too.”
“Well, once we find her, Itsuki needs to be turned back to normal, after all.”
“I imagine Ren-san wants to return to normal too.”
“Itsuki, what about you, though?”
“I’m not particularly interested in returning to normal, honestly. I don’t feel much benefit in going back to being a so-called superior being, a human.”
It seemed Itsuki had rather taken a liking to his riska form.
